packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-05 - unverified blind image reading (reader D)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of the fragment's text was in my context.
- image-013.jpg shows the printed title page of the HOST volume (an Italian
  printed book with a Venice imprint). This is visible in the supplied images
  and identifies the host book, not the fragment. I did not use it for reading.
- Beyond the brief: I made contrast-enhanced greyscale copies, and mirrored
  copies, of tiles 002, 003, 004, 008, 010, 011, 012 in my own scratchpad
  folder (readerD/) to try to read faint strokes. No other files opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, front cover) and image-007 (overview, back cover): a
  limp parchment wrapper. A vertical parchment strip (c. 4-5 cm wide visible)
  from a manuscript leaf runs along the spine side, between a grey paper
  repair panel and the main cover parchment. Ink is very abraded / faded
  brown; only the strip's width of each line is visible (perhaps 6-10
  letters per line), the rest is covered by the cover turn-in or paper.
- Alternating red and blue lombard-style initials, each 1-2 lines high, at
  the left edge of the text block with pen-flourish extensions (red with blue
  penwork, blue with red penwork). Initials seen: blue C/E-shaped (001 top),
  blue I (001 top / 006), red C/E-shaped (004), red R (004), blue initial
  (001 lower; 003 frame), on the back: blue I/L and blue D (008), red R and
  red E/C (010, mirrored), blue square bracket-like frame (003, 011).
- Initials recur every few lines, which suggests (tentatively) short items
  such as verses/versicles, but I cannot confirm this from the crop.
- image-010 and image-011 (back cover) show text and initials MIRROR-REVERSED.
  Mirroring 010 gives the same layout as 004 (red C/E-shaped initial over a
  red R). I take 010/011 to be the same strip area seen through the
  parchment or as an offset, not additional text. Treat as overlap.
- image-012: upper part of back strip, top margin blank, then faint lines.
- image-014: spine, paper/parchment lining with one line of dark brown text
  and a line in red ink below; heavily wormed. Script there looks larger.
- No running titles, no glosses or marginalia visible.

READINGS
The ink is so abraded that no word could be read with confidence. Letter
groups below are offered only as shapes; every one is uncertain.

image-004.jpg (front strip, middle; counted from top of tile)
  l.1-3   [illegible] (traces only)
  l.4     red initial C or E (2-line) followed by [illegible]
  l.5-9   [illegible] (white abrasion stain across lines)
  l.10    [illegible] ...re? / ...ce?
  l.11    red initial R + [illegible] ...e?
  l.12    R(cont.) ...oo? / ...os? hem? or b(e)m? [illegible]
  l.13    ...nur? / ...mir? [illegible]
  l.14    ...ma? [illegible]
  l.15-   [illegible]

image-003.jpg (front strip, lower)
  l.1-6   [illegible]
  l.7     blue initial traces (pale, round) [illegible]
  l.8     ...rie? / ...cie? [illegible]
  l.9     ...nis? ...pib(us)? [illegible]
  l.10    [illegible]
  l.11    red round initial (O/C?) + [illegible] ...o
  l.12    ...ac? [illegible]
  l.13    blue frame line of an initial; then ...no? [illegible]
  l.14    ...ncis? / ...mcle? [illegible]

image-002.jpg (front strip, lower): about 8-9 lines, all [illegible]; the
  last line ends in shapes like ...lieue? / ...ietie? (very uncertain); below
  it blank parchment (lower margin or end of text block).

image-006.jpg (front strip, top): about 4 lines before a blue C/E initial,
  then a blue I initial with red penwork 3 lines lower; all text [illegible].

image-008.jpg (back strip): blue I/L initial and blue D initial with red
  penwork on the right edge (adjacent to the cover edge); text to their
  left [illegible].

image-012.jpg (back strip top): blank top area, then c. 6 lines; first
  readable shape ...uniue? / ...iuuare? (mirrored? uncertain), rest
  [illegible].

image-014.jpg (spine lining): brown ink line: ...nu... [illegible];
  red ink line below: fra? ... 7? ... (could be a later label, uncertain).

AREAS UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Effectively all text remains unread; the gaps reflect the state of the ink,
  not unviewed tiles. Each tile was examined at native size and enhanced.
- Line counts are approximate because the ruling is invisible.
- Only the strip width is exposed; line ends/beginnings beyond the turn-in
  are hidden.
SUGGESTIONS
- Multispectral or UV imaging of the strip; or imaging from inside the cover
  if the turn-in can be lifted (the mirrored text in 010/011 suggests the
  ink is visible from the other side too). Raking light on 003/004.
